mere-fidelity.title: Measuring Wealth
mere-fidelity.description: How can each subsequent generation both be making more money and be considerably less wealthy? The answer is obvious. The solution may not be.

christians-reading-classics.title: The Idiot by Fyodor Dostoevsky with Maria Baer
christians-reading-classics.description: A foggy train pulls into St Petersburg and two young men face each other across a third-class carriage. That opening scene from Dostoevsky’s The Idiot is our doorway into a novel that refuses to let anyone stay comfortable, especially when a pure-hearted man starts telling the truth in rooms built on performance. Nadia Williams talks with writer and reporter Maria Baer to talk about why 21st-century American Christians should still read this translated Russian classic. We dig into what makes a “classic” more than a school requirement, how to pick a translation that actually keeps you turning pages, and why reading older books helps us notice the invisible norms shaping our own lives.
